material_points: Material finding of this batch: the Guide adopts the cursor, subscription and queued-decision members of IDR-040's 'cannot outlive its policy/trust bounds' invariant but not the cache member. It emits strong ETags (line 503) and Vary (line 739), names RFC 9110/9111 as an inherited dependency (line 258), and nowhere binds a validator or cache key to the authorized view, specifies any Cache-Control directive, or lists a cache channel among its disclosure tests (1019, 983). RFC 9111 Section 3.5 protects only requests carrying an Authorization header, Section 5.2.2.7's private directive is never invoked, and Section 4.1 keys Vary selection only on nominated request header fields. Two concrete consequences: a validator computed over stored state rather than the emitted authorized representation becomes an inference channel for concealed changes; and in the trusted-reverse-proxy deployments the Guide supports (364, 596), where authorization derives from a client certificate or a proxy-injected header rather than an Authorization header, an intermediary may serve one caller's authorized representation to another context. Bounded fix: one Guide sentence plus one added test-list entry. Recorded under F-03 (whose residual question is already selected concealment semantics), not as a competing finding number.

reuse_rules: Batch 17 reviews the common issue boilerplate once and every distinct variant; batches 19-26 never re-check it.

Batch 17 compares all 286 issues task-specific content against their Roadmap leaves mechanically. Content that matches an already-read leaf is reused by batches 19-26, not reviewed twice; only the difference inventory and the scope and acceptance accounting carry forward. CLARIFIED IN ITERATION 36: reuse means one shared copy of the matching text is assessed once and its assessment carried to every task that shares it. It does NOT mean matching content is exempt from semantic review. Mechanical equality established in batch 17 shows the text was copied faithfully; it says nothing about whether the scope and acceptance are adequate against the Guide and the findings.

For the six partial reports (IDR-006, IDR-007, IDR-010, IDR-014B, IDR-017, IDR-044), the existing evidence is reused and only the unread key sections are screened, inside the cluster batch that already covers their topic. A partial read does not establish complete coverage.
